text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging sara (oncall) — elevated 5xx rate on hosted API; global 5xx = 7.8% over 2m, queue depth on runtime nodes > 1200 (norm ~300). Auto-escalation to eng-oncall.

sara (oncall): seeing it, joining. any obvious deploys?

evan: no recent prod deploys in last 30m. Autoscaling appears healthy but tails are blowing up. Logs show repeated 'KVCache OOM' + timeouts in runtime.

liam: hit from customer traffic spikes? spikes from a handful of API keys — top 3 keys account for ~42% of requests in last 5m.

cindy (support): support reports 3 customers complaining about timeouts and partial responses. raising impact to P2 for those customers.

jordan (sre): priority mitigation plan: 1) apply tenant-level rate limits for noisy keys, 2) lower global max-in-flight to reduce queueing pressure, 3) enable shedding for low-priority model variants, 4) shorten request timeouts to free stuck workers, 5) disable experimental reranker to cut per-request CPU.

sara (oncall): agree. i'll start with a soft global cap change and a quick tenant throttle. i'm going to run the admin API call.

sara (oncall): executing:
```
# set global max-in-flight from 2000 -> 1200
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood-inference.local/runtime/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"runtime.max_in_flight":1200}'
```

ops-bot: config update accepted (txn 0x7f4d), rolling to runtime nodes.

sara (oncall): applying temporary tenant throttle for top noisy keys (reduce qps to 40% of baseline).

sara (oncall): command:
```
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood-inference.local/tenants/throttle" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"keys": ["key_ABC","key_XYZ","key_123"], "qps_factor": 0.4, "duration_seconds": 900}'
```

evan: also enable shedding for rerankers and low-priority backends:
```
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood-inference.local/runtime/shedding" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"variants": ["reranker-v2","aux-embedder"], "policy": "probabilistic", "prob": 0.5}'
```

jordan (sre): lowering per-request timeout from 60s -> 30s for generation routes to recover stuck in-flight workers.

liam: done. routes updated.

incident-bot: action log:
- max_in_flight: 2000 -> 1200 (initiated by sara)
- tenant throttles applied to 3 keys (40% qps for 15m)
- shedding enabled for reranker-v2/aux-embedder (50%)
- route timeout: generation 60s -> 30s
- disabled feature flag: experimental-rerank (ff:exp_rerank = false)

cindy (support): letting impacted customers know we're throttling noisy keys and working on broader mitigation. sending templated note now.

sara (oncall): monitoring dashboards — queue depth dropping to ~420 in 3m, 5xx rate down to 2.1%. CPU on runtime nodes back in safer range. good sign.

evan: one noisy key still shows spike; traffic seems retrying aggressively. recommend adding short-circuit 429-based backoff to clients (we can return Retry-After).

sara (oncall): pushing 429 + Retry-After header for throttled tenants now.

ops-bot: tenant throttle responses: 429 served for 97% of requests from key_ABC in last 60s; retries decreased.

jordan (sre): after these changes, P95 latency dropped from 1.8s -> 1.1s, 99th from 8.5s -> 4.0s. request success rate improved.

liam: can we enable a temporary fallback routing rule to route non-critical traffic to a cheaper lower-cap model (latency optimized) to free capacity?

sara (oncall): yes — activating routing policy for non-enterprise customers: route model: text-gen-large -> text-gen-medium for read-only workloads.

sara (oncall): command:
```
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood-inference.local/routing/policy" -d '{"selector":"tier!=enterprise","from":"text-gen-large","to":"text-gen-medium","duration_seconds":1800}'
```

incident-bot: routing policy pushed.

cindy (support): customers on tickets report partial recovery; marking impacted tickets "mitigated" for now.

evan: we should capture metrics for postmortem: per-tenant qps, retry rates, queue depth, max_in_flight config history, and shedding decisions. create follow-up action items.

sara (oncall): agreed. i'm going to handoff to evan in 20m. leaving notes:
- actions taken (config txn, tenant throttles, shedding, timeout/routing changes)
- temporary windows: throttles 15m, routing 30m, config rollback plan if regressions.

sara (oncall): @evan — you have the incident in 20. will stay available if anything spikes. :white_check_mark:

evan: taking handoff. i'll keep monitoring and start an RCA draft once stable. please add any logs or screenshots to the incident doc.

jordan (sre): follow-ups: 1) make throttling automation for noisy tenants (policy + thresholds), 2) implement graceful shedding metrics, 3) review default max_in_flight and autoscaler interplay, 4) enforce client-side backoff guidance in SDK.

cindy (support): coordinating customer comms for the affected accounts, will post updates when we move to postmortem.

incident-bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. SLA impact: partial (some requests were 429/timeout). Page closed for oncall rotation.

sara (oncall): closing thread for now. good team work, nice quick mitigations.

evan: noted. will run postmortem template and tag SRE/Runtime/DevEx.

liam: adding one last note — we should consider dynamic tenant scoring to proactively throttle before queue pressure spikes.

sara (oncall): agreed. adding as action item.

ops-bot: reminder scheduled: create incident doc in #incidents with tag "runtime-backpressure" in 30m.

jordan (sre): thanks everyone.
